subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Lu Yu and The Classic of Tea
description: One-minute skill: Lu Yu and The Classic of Tea.

hook.text: In 760 AD, an orphan raised by monks wrote the world's first book entirely about tea.

buildup.text: Lu Yu's 'Cha Jing' (The Classic of Tea) covered growing, processing, brewing, and drinking tea.

discovery.text: He described 28 pieces of tea equipment and insisted on specific water sources and precise boiling stages.

twist.text: Lu Yu elevated tea from a simple drink to an art form with philosophy, aesthetics, and ritual.

climax.text: His book made him a cultural hero. Tea merchants kept statues of Lu Yu in their shops for good luck.

punchline.text: One orphan's book turned brewing tea into high art.

quiz.question: What was Lu Yu's 'Cha Jing'?
options: The world's first book dedicated to tea

details.summary: Lu Yu wrote the Cha Jing, or Classic of Tea, around 760 CE, the world's first known book on tea. It covered cultivation, processing, brewing equipment, and proper preparation. Lu Yu elevated tea from a simple drink to an art form and is revered as the patron saint of tea.
details.whyItMatters: The Classic of Tea codified tea culture and gave it intellectual respectability. It is the founding document for treating tea as worthy of serious study and practice.
takeaways: Lu Yu wrote the world's first tea book around 760 CE
The Cha Jing covered growing, processing, and brewing
Lu Yu is revered as the patron saint of tea

faq.question: What did the Classic of Tea actually contain?
faq.answer: It covered ten chapters: the origins of the tea plant, tools for picking and processing, types of tea, utensils for preparation, methods of brewing, drinking etiquette, historical references, growing regions, and occasions for simplifying the ritual. It was encyclopedic for its time.

faq.question: Who was Lu Yu and why was he so influential?
faq.answer: Lu Yu was an orphan raised by Buddhist monks who became a scholar and tea master. His meticulous observation and elegant writing elevated tea appreciation into a respected discipline. His work influenced tea culture for over a millennium and remains studied today.
